clue.text: Cocktail of wine duly hard to handle

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the following words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drink made from wine turns out to be awkward to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cumbersome or awkward to manage is hard to handle, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: As tune changes, remove an MP, perhaps

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the preceding two words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: As the song alters, a member of parliament is turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: To unseat an MP is to make them lose their seat in Parliament at an election; 'perhaps' marks the MP as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Depriving an elected member of their seat is the political sense of the verb.

clue.text: Sink was given nasty bash at home

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so the letters of bash are scrambled

parts.note: at home means in, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A kitchen sink got a vicious whack in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' is the anagram signal and shuffles the letters of 'bash'; 'Sink' is the noun, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin with taps for washing hands is a bathroom sink, so the noun fits directly.

clue.text: Perform in river? Lovely

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
lovely in the sense of sweet and attractive means cute

explanation.surface: Someone asks if putting on a show in the river would be delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England, flowing through Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a manoeuvre or plan is to carry it out, a synonym for perform.

clue.text: Odd odes and singular measures

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, hinting that the word odes is jumbled

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Strange poems and one-off yardsticks sit together in a peculiar list.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses are measured quantities of medicine, so measures as a plural noun fits.

clue.text: Cost of maintenance of high castle tower

parts.note: high means up, as in up in the air
the keep is the main fortified tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Someone asks what it costs to look after a lofty castle tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the expense of keeping something in good repair, so it names that cost.

clue.text: Peaceful — or perhaps loco?

definitions.meaning: calm and tranquil, the sense that gave the ocean its name
a type of steam locomotive with a 4-6-2 wheel arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a person is calm or simply crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like slang for mad, but it is short for locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tranquil, and is also the name of a class of steam engine.

clue.text: Issue as former partner getting cuddles on a regular basis

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: on a regular basis means taking every other letter of the word cuddles, starting with the second

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is handing out hugs every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue as a verb means to flow or ooze out, as liquid seeping from a surface.

clue.text: Mine's the best of places for rapid vehicle maintenance

parts.note: mine means pit, and the 's adds S
the tops means the very best, as in it's the tops

explanation.surface: A boast that one's own garage is the finest for quick car repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive pronoun but is the noun for a colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, cars pull into these brief halts for tyres and fuel during a race.

clue.text: Kit often seen with this in taxi — a lot? Almost

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for plenty is left off

parts.note: oodles means a lot, plenty

explanation.surface: A huge load of gear is crammed into a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' is not equipment here but part of the phrase 'the whole kit and caboodle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'the whole kit and caboodle' pairs the two words, so the definition points to the partner word.

clue.text: Thrilling tale: unknown items recorded here?

definitions.meaning: a story full of tension is a ..., read as two words
in bookkeeping, entries whose proper place is not yet known are parked in a temporary ledger

explanation.surface: A gripping story is offered alongside a place for logging mysteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants use this temporary ledger for transactions not yet classified, and literally it is a narrative full of tension.

clue.text: Shelters not opened in these pleasant garden spots

indicators.note: not opened means the first letter of the word for shelters is removed

parts.note: harbours are places of shelter

explanation.surface: Covered places that have never been unlocked are lovely nooks in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowers shaded by trees or climbing plants are pleasant shady retreats in a garden.

clue.text: Unorthodox and rotten cricketer restricting English

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten

indicators.note: restricting means the cricketer surrounds and confines the letter for English

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: An unconventional and useless cricketer keeps an Englishman in check.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'bat' is a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or quirky, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Went up as century came to a close

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence century
came to a close means ended

explanation.surface: Something rose just as the hundred years finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or rise is to go up, the simple past matching 'went'.

clue.text: Get less iron, one could say?

definitions.meaning: to get less is to diminish or shrink
ironing removes creases, so read as ... it means take creases out

explanation.surface: A puzzled request for less iron in one's diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' looks like the mineral but is the verb for pressing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means shrink, and split as de-crease it playfully means flattening out wrinkles.

clue.text: Car, primarily an old banger, not costing a lot

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word car is used

parts.note: a heap is a dilapidated old car

explanation.surface: A car that's essentially a wreck shouldn't cost much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' is British slang for a battered old car, as is 'heap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexpensive costs little money, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lively quote half-hearted author's written up

indicators.note: written up means, in a down entry, the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two letters at the heart of the author's name is dropped

parts.note: Graham Greene is the author, with 's linking him to what follows

explanation.surface: A quotation from a tepid writer is printed in a spirited style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one E from the middle pair of GREENE to give GRENE; 'written up' reverses CITEGRENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of energy and vigour is lively, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Arrives at rim to see rockfall?

parts.note: an aircraft that lands arrives
the lip of a cup is its rim

explanation.surface: Someone reaches a cliff edge only to witness a collapse of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslip is a slide of earth and rock down a slope, much like a rockfall.

clue.text: The top's come off loudspeaker — bother!

indicators.note: the top's come off means the first letter of the word for the loudspeaker is removed

parts.note: Tannoy is a British brand name for a public address loudspeaker system

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry as the cover falls off a public address speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: TANNOY is the British trade name used for any public address system.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother someone is to irritate or pester them, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: At last, Harry gets what's deserved and longed for

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of the word Harry is taken

parts.note: what is earned is what one deserves

explanation.surface: Harry finally receives his just reward, something he had wished for.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yearned is to have desired or pined for something deeply.

clue.text: Men gathered for a board meeting?

definitions.text: Men gathered for a board meeting?

parts.words: Men gathered for a board meeting?
parts.note: chess pieces are called men, and they are set out together on a board for a game

explanation.surface: Executives assemble for a company board meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' suggests directors, but the board is a chessboard and the men are pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A full set of chessmen is assembled whenever two players meet over the board.

clue.text: Any number in goal maybe, with Germany held in contempt

indicators.note: in means the letter for any number is placed inside the word for a goal

parts.note: a goal is an example of a score in football
N stands for any number in mathematics
D is the international vehicle registration code for Germany

explanation.surface: Germany is derided for any goals it manages to put away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scorned means being treated with disdain, which is the same as held in contempt.

clue.text: Publicity material with alternative directions for ornaments

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity material
or is the word that introduces an alternative
N and S are the compass directions north and south

explanation.surface: A brochure offers different routes to find some decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornaments' is a verb here, meaning decorates.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn something is to decorate it, so ornaments as a third-person verb matches.

clue.text: Dull brown, new-age material found in ship's hold

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
new gives N, the abbreviation, and age is used as written

explanation.surface: Drab brown hippy fabric is discovered stored below a vessel's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunnage is loose packing such as matting or timber used to protect cargo stowed in a hold.

clue.text: New diamonds, right? That's better!

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Fresh diamonds, correct? That's an improvement!
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer means more pleasant, a comparative just like better.

clue.text: Female made a record — it's sold

parts.note: to log something is to make a record of it

explanation.surface: A woman notes down that an item has been sold.
explanation.walkthrough: To flog is informal British slang for to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Flogged is British slang for sold, as in flogged the car to a dealer.

clue.text: Bone incorporated into life mural

indicators.note: incorporated into means the letters sit inside the phrase life mural

explanation.surface: An anatomical bone is painted into a mural depicting life.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone is the longest bone in the human body, an example of a bone.

clue.text: Men with horns closest to fight mythical creature

indicators.note: to fight suggests a scrap or brawl, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Stags with nearest antlers lock horns in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins MEN to HORNS CLOSEST as one pool of fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the legendary beast said to live in a Scottish lake, a famous creature of myth.

clue.text: Standard achieved without Mike in street procession

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: without means the letter for Mike is taken away from the word for achieved

parts.note: to have made it is to have achieved
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: A normal standard is reached without a microphone at a street march.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a public procession through the streets, a synonym for that march.

clue.text: In favour of pipes and various manufactured items

parts.note: pro means in favour of
ducts are pipes or channels

explanation.surface: Someone supports plumbing and assorted factory goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made in factories are products, the plural noun matching assorted items.
